work: King Wan As Son And Heir
heading: Liji 6 · Wen Wang Shizi 文王世子 · King Wan As Son And Heir · Wen Wang Shizi II.19 … Wen Wang Shizi II.24

items.text: Morning and evening, ask the attendant inside the door whether his father is well and how he is.
items.quote: Morning and evening he went to the outside of the door of the great chamber, and asked the attendant of the interior whether his father were well

items.text: Show joy in his countenance when his father is well; show sorrow and disturbed demeanour when he is ill; resume his former appearance when he is better.
items.quote: If told that he was well, his joy appeared in his countenance. ... his sorrow and anxiety appeared

items.text: Morning and evening when food is sent up, examine whether it is hot or cold as it ought to be.
items.quote: Morning and evening when the food went up, he would examine it and see if it were hot or cold as it ought to be.

items.text: After the food comes down, ask what his father has eaten.
items.quote: When it came down, he asked what his father had eaten.

items.text: Know what viands go in and give his orders to the cook; then retire.
items.quote: He made it a point to know what viands went in, and to give his orders to the cook; and then he retired.

items.text: If his father is ill, fast and personally wait on him in dark-coloured dress.
items.quote: If the attendant reported that his father was ill, then he himself fasted and waited on him in his dark-coloured dress.

items.text: Inspect with reverence the food prepared by the cook, and taste the medicine himself before giving it to his father.
items.quote: He inspected with reverence the food prepared by the cook, and tasted himself the medicine for the patient.

items.text: If his father eats well, then he may eat; if his father eats little, he must not take a full meal.
items.quote: If his father ate well of the food, then he was able to eat. If his father ate but little, then he could not take a full meal.

work: King Wan As Son And Heir
heading: Liji 6 · Wen Wang Shizi 文王世子 · King Wan As Son And Heir · Wen Wang Shizi I.1 … Wen Wang Shizi I.16

items.text: Visit your father three times a day to ask after his health and well-being.
items.quote: Thrice a day he made a visit in due form to king Kî.

items.text: If your father is unwell, let your sorrow show in your face and your walk be disturbed.
items.quote: If the king were not so well as usual, the servant would tell the prince, and then his sorrow appeared in his countenance, and his walk was affected and disturbed.

items.text: Examine the food served to your father to ensure it is properly hot or cold, and after he has eaten ask what dishes he had and order the cook not to serve them again.
items.quote: When the food went up (to the king), he would examine it and see if it were cold and hot as it ought to be. When it came down, he asked of what dishes the king had eaten. He gave orders to the cook that none of the dishes should go up again.

items.text: When your father is ill, nurse him without removing your cap or girdle, remaining constantly ready.
items.quote: When king Wan was ill, Wû nursed him without taking off his cap or girdle.

items.text: Eat only when your father eats, following his meal times.
items.quote: When king Wan took a meal, he also took a meal; and when king Wan took a second, he did the same.

items.text: Correct and discipline your son when he errs, so that he may learn proper conduct.
items.quote: When he committed an error, the duke punished Po-khin.

items.text: Instruct the young heir in his duties, using the discipline of your own child as an example.
items.quote: He illustrated the rules for the behaviour of a young heir in his treatment of Po-khin, that king Khang might thereby know the courses to be pursued by father and son, ruler and minister, old and young.

work: King Wan As Son And Heir
heading: Liji 6 · Wen Wang Shizi 文王世子 · King Wan As Son And Heir · Wen Wang Shizi I.17 … Wen Wang Shizi II.5

items.text: Give your father the affection due him, and honor him as father.
items.quote: If the son can give the affection due to the father, and the honour due to the ruler

items.text: Practice filial piety toward your parents: obey, respect, and care for them.
items.quote: inculcated on them filial piety and fraternal duty

items.text: Honor your elder siblings and observe the duties of a younger brother or sister.
items.quote: fraternal duty

items.text: Yield precedence to uncles and aunts as your elders, no matter what rank you hold.
items.quote: he did not take precedence of an uncle or elder cousin.

items.text: Younger cousins, yield to your elder cousins as to age, deferring to them in seating and order.
items.quote: he did not take precedence of an uncle or elder cousin.

items.text: Give the eldest son of the primary wife precedence in temple rites; other sons must yield.
items.quote: the eldest son by the wife took the precedence.

work: King Wan As Son And Heir
heading: Liji 6 · Wen Wang Shizi 文王世子 · King Wan As Son And Heir · Wen Wang Shizi II.6 … Wen Wang Shizi II.18

items.text: Guard the spirit-tablets and ancestral temples; let the eldest sons guard the temple of the Grand ancestor, the uncles guard the most honored shrines, and the other sons and grandsons guard the inferior shrines.
items.quote: the kindred guarded the spirit-tablets... the eldest sons by the proper wives guarding the temple of the Grand ancestor
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the First Commandment and the sole mediatorship of Christ.

items.text: Announce cappings, marriages, and deaths to the ancestral temple of the Grand ancestor.
items.quote: All descended from any of the five rulers... were required to announce the events of capping and marriage... Their deaths had to be announced
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the First Commandment and the sole mediatorship of Christ.

items.text: Observe the rules for condoling, for wearing or removing the mourning cap, and for presenting mourning gifts.
items.quote: the regulations for condoling and not condoling, leaving off and not leaving off the cap... and the correct rules for the mourning gifts

items.text: Do not subject a kinsman to castration, lest the family line be cut off.
items.quote: No one of the ruler's kindred was punished with castration.

items.text: When a kinsman is executed, wear white, refrain from a full meal and music, and wail privately in a temple of a different surname; but do not wear mourning or offer public condolence.
items.quote: he put on white clothes, and did not have a full meal or music... the ruler did not wear mourning, but wailed for him himself

items.text: At inner-court receptions, take places according to age, not rank, to maintain the father-son relation among kinsmen.
items.quote: they took places according to their age, even those among them of high rank, showed the relation to be maintained between father and son.

items.text: In the ancestral temple, ascend first, take precedence in partaking of the offerings, and receive the cup to honor the ancestor.
items.quote: the eldest son by the proper wife was employed to ascend, take precedence in partaking of what had been left, and in receiving the cup
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the First Commandment and the sole mediatorship of Christ.

items.text: Wear mourning robes according to the closeness of kinship, not lessening the degree of relationship.
items.quote: the distinctions at the funeral rites were arranged according to the fineness or coarseness of their mourning robes

items.text: At feasts with kinsmen, take seats according to age and generation, with each lower generation taking a lower place, to cultivate filial piety and fraternal duty.
items.quote: The ruler, when feasting with his kindred, took his place among them according to age... each generation took a lower place as it was removed a degree from the parent-stem

items.text: Punish an offending kinsman secretly, not in public with common people.
items.quote: the offender was punished in secret, and not associated with common people
